shared_elements: rows of overlapping feathers rendered as repeated scale-like/curved units
tightly curled locks of hair or mane in regular rows
profile head with large detailed eye and modelled brow
low-relief figure carved on a flat slab
fringed/tasselled edging of textile or plumage
dense linear incised patterning covering large areas of the body
justification: Both surfaces show a large low-relief winged being whose plumage is rendered as stacked rows of identical curved feather units and whose hair/mane is a grid of tight spiral curls, with fringed edges and a heavy profile head with an emphatic eye and brow — an unusually specific set of shared carving conventions. The main difference in content is that A shows an animal (bovine/leonine) head in close view with the wing sweeping behind it, while B shows a full standing human-bodied figure with a raised arm, garment and handled bucket, so the figural composition and attributes do not correspond.
